routeSelection.route: Film and Music with Analysis and Criticism
routeSelection.basis: The example selects the first two departmental arts disciplines listed in the regulations, Film and Music, and the cross-arts Analysis and Criticism framework. Faculty-wide and other choices use the order in the regulations, independently of UCR course fit.

selection.assessment: Three coherent options reach the maximum. Art and cultural analysis is the closest. Film, literature and communication, and arts policy and enterprise, give greater weight to distinct interests. The options differ by 45, 97.5 and 112.5 EC each way. Music and theatre remain evidenced directions outside construction.

alternatives.label: Arts, Media and Cultural Analysis
alternatives.labelReason: Art history, film and literature introduce methods before art historiography, adaptation and documentary. Sociology precedes qualitative research.
alternatives.concept: Study how art, literature and media shape public life. Combine art history, museum studies, film analysis and sociology to investigate how creative works acquire meaning and whose perspectives they represent.
progression: Art history, film and literature introduce methods before art historiography, adaptation and documentary. Sociology precedes qualitative research.

alternatives.label: Literature, Film and Cultural Communication
alternatives.labelReason: Introductory film, literature and rhetoric support film adaptation, media histories, documentary and experimental writing.
alternatives.concept: Study how stories move between literature, film and other media. Analyse texts and screen works, then practise documentary, rhetoric and experimental writing to see how different forms address audiences.
alternatives.distinctness: Film, narrative, rhetoric, popular media and creative communication carry more weight.
progression: Introductory film, literature and rhetoric support film adaptation, media histories, documentary and experimental writing.

alternatives.label: Arts Policy, Culture and Entrepreneurship
alternatives.labelReason: Economics and business foundations support public economics, marketing and research. Museum, media and heritage courses ground the study of arts institutions.
alternatives.concept: Study how arts organisations reach audiences, make decisions and respond to public policy. Combine cultural study with economics, market research, entrepreneurship and analysis of digital change.
progression: Economics and business foundations support public economics, marketing and research. Museum, media and heritage courses ground the study of arts institutions.
alternatives.distinctness: Economics, enterprise, organisational behaviour, market research and public policy carry more weight.

blocks: Students complete 30 EC of approved minor or study abroad.
Groningen requires a thesis after completion of the second year. At UCR, independent research is optional.
Arts, film, media, literature and heritage
Both study how art is selected and exhibited for audiences. UCR also surveys modern art and museum practice.
Both study how artistic forms make meaning. UCR focuses on literary interpretation, while Groningen brings several art forms together.
Both examine narrative across forms, including text, images and performance. UCR focuses on myth.
Both examine how stories shape identity. UCR focuses on memoir and travel writing.
Both examine relationships between media. UCR studies those relationships through film adaptation.
Both introduce film form and teach close analysis of images, sound, editing and narrative.
Both combine practical work and reflection. UCR focuses on making a documentary, while Groningen’s projects depend on the chosen arts profile.
This course surveys film, television, music and the performing arts together.
Groningen introduces analysis of classical and popular music.
Groningen requires a dedicated survey of film history. UCR’s film introduction includes selected historical movements.
Groningen continues with the history and theory of classical music.
This example uses the faculty-wide course on storytelling.
Groningen requires a dedicated film theory course. UCR applies theory in film, adaptation and documentary courses.
Students read professional arts criticism and write reviews for public audiences.
This example uses the advanced film seminar, which requires Film III.
Both introduce social theory and institutions. Groningen applies them specifically to the arts.
Arts policy, organisations and cultural entrepreneurship

notes.text: Groningen’s Film and Music example has dedicated sequences in both disciplines, followed by arts practice and a thesis. UCR offers related courses in film, literature, visual art and cultural research. Its courses cover some performance and sound topics, with no comparable music or theatre sequence.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

audience.programmeDescription: Arts, Culture and Media at the University of Groningen studies how art is made, interpreted and shared. This example combines Film and Music with the Analysis and Criticism framework.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines cultural analysis with visual art, film and literature. Other options focus on storytelling across media or on arts organisations and policy. Groningen offers a dedicated music sequence and requires a thesis.
